## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-fascicle Tang-period translation by **Amoghavajra** ([不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA)) of the *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī* (大孔雀明王 *Dàkǒngquè míngwáng*) — the goddess-spell of the Great Peacock who guards against snake-bite, fever, and demonic affliction. The text is the standard Tang Esoteric recension of the *Mahāmāyūrī* and superseded the earlier translations by Kumārajīva ([KR6j0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0175)), Saṅghapāla ([KR6j0171](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0171)), Yìjìng ([KR6j0172](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0172)), and the anonymous early-medieval recensions ([KR6j0173](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0173)–[KR6j0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0174)). Together with the *Mahāmegha-sūtra* (大雲經 [KR6j0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0176)–[KR6j0180](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0180)), the *Mahāmāyūrī* belongs to the cluster of *vidyārājñī*-protective scriptures that constituted one of the principal pillars of Tang state Buddhism.
